description: Card P's targets for "3.8 L pushrod V6": the invariants are hard; the rest are reported, never failed: their misses are the simulator's to-do list. Predicted strongest lines (not measured: the validation format has no line measure yet): the firing frequency, rpm/60 x 6/2, 32.5 Hz at the 650 rpm idle and 285 Hz at the 5700 rpm limiter.

targets.name: Invariant: starts warm and runs
targets.source: a warm engine started on its key runs and keeps running (engine.state 2)

targets.name: Invariant: within full scale
targets.source: 02-contracts.md, section 1: what process writes is within +-1

targets.name: Sound: a free rev is loud enough
targets.source: the lead's ruling (20:11): at a build's defaults a free rev peaks at 0.3 to 0.6 of full scale; under 0.2 is too quiet to hear the work (L's listener at 23 to 30 dB under the reference mix: L's finding)

targets.name: Sound: the idle is audible
targets.source: the lead's ruling (20:11): the idle plainly audible: its level over 8 to 14 s at least -40 dB of full scale (judgement: a quiet room's background against a full-scale peak)

targets.name: Invariant: holds its limiter
targets.source: a rev limiter holds the speed within a few percent of where it cuts (some 100 to 200 rpm at 6500)

targets.name: Invariant: pulls away
targets.source: started, in gear and on the pedal, the car moves (a 36 t tractor in third of eighteen at least 1.5 m/s)

targets.name: Invariant: stops at the key
targets.source: the key off stops the engine (engine.state 0 by the run's end)

targets.name: Starts cold
targets.source: a sound engine starts from the air's temperature within some four seconds of cranking and keeps running (a rule of thumb; makers' cold-start specifications are 2 to 5 s)

targets.name: Peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures of the 1990s, firm): 3791 cc; 37 to 42 kW a litre; looked up: 3800wiki.com/overview (153 kW at 5200, 312 N m at 4000); Wikipedia's GM 3800 (205 hp, 230 lb ft)

targets.name: Speed at peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures of the 1990s, firm): 3791 cc: 5000 to 5400 rpm; looked up: 3800wiki.com/overview (153 kW at 5200, 312 N m at 4000); Wikipedia's GM 3800 (205 hp, 230 lb ft)

targets.name: Peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures of the 1990s, firm): 3791 cc; BMEP 9.9 to 10.9 bar (a naturally aspirated petrol engine 10 to 13 bar, turbocharged 18 to 25, a modern truck diesel 20 to 25: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 2); looked up: 3800wiki.com/overview (153 kW at 5200, 312 N m at 4000); Wikipedia's GM 3800 (205 hp, 230 lb ft)

targets.name: Speed at peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (makers' figures of the 1990s, firm): 3791 cc: 3800 to 4200 rpm (a turbocharged engine's plateau: its whole span); looked up: 3800wiki.com/overview (153 kW at 5200, 312 N m at 4000); Wikipedia's GM 3800 (205 hp, 230 lb ft)

targets.name: Warm idle
targets.source: makers' service specifications of the kind: 600 to 750 rpm warm in neutral (a rule of thumb, firm to 100 rpm); the ECU is asked for 650

targets.name: Idle steadiness
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb): its highest point from 6 to 14 s more than 100 rpm over the 650 rpm asked is a hunt

targets.name: Idle low point
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb): its lowest point from 6 to 14 s more than 100 rpm under the 650 rpm asked is a hunt (or a stall coming)

targets.name: Volumetric efficiency at its torque peak
targets.source: a naturally aspirated four-stroke's VE at full load near its torque peak is 0.85 to 1.0 (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 6, fig. 6-9 and the text); measured at 4000 rpm

targets.name: Volumetric efficiency low down
targets.source: VE's shape: below the torque peak it falls away, the more so the hotter the cam (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 6); measured at 2000 rpm

targets.name: Port gas at full load
targets.source: what a thermocouple at the exhaust port reads at full load (a time mean, below the gas's mass mean): some 1100 to 1300 K for a spark-ignition engine (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14; card C's target on default.json); tel.exhaust.portThermocouple, card G's mixing cup

targets.name: Header gas at full load
targets.source: a thermocouple a little way down a primary reads 900 to 1100 K at full load on a petrol engine (JUDGEMENT from memory of makers' exhaust-gas-temperature data, not a cited full-load figure: under review, the lead's question of 20:17; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14); tel.exhaust.headerThermocouple

targets.name: Port gas, mass mean (information)
targets.source: the gas's mass (enthalpy) mean at the port, kept for information: above a thermocouple's reading, not a target (card G, f703892)

targets.name: Quarter mile: time
targets.source: Hale's rule, ET = 5.825 (lb/hp)^(1/3) s, with the kind's published power (150 kW) and the build's mass: 15.29 s; 5 % quicker to 15 % slower for the build's own tyres and launch (card I's test holds drag radials to 8 %)

targets.name: Quarter mile: trap speed
targets.source: Hale's rule, trap = 234 (hp/lb)^(1/3) mph: 39.9 m/s (143 km/h), within 8 % under to 6 % over

targets.name: Top speed
targets.source: where 0.85 of the kind's published power (150 kW) meets the build's drag area and 1.2 % rolling resistance at 1.225 kg/m^3: 230 km/h, within 7 % (a power balance, not a test)
